recap.workouts:
Nothing ridden and nothing run today, and that was a decision rather than a fade.

RT19 was the only thing on the sheet — no gym on a Sunday — and your note says it straight: still not completely recovered from the illness, so running it would have been pointless. I agree with you, and I want to say why rather than just nodding. This plan's own rule for a retest that arrives on a bad day is to MOVE it, never to water it down, because a half-executed tune block costs the full fatigue, produces a number anyway, and that number then prescribes the next nine weeks. Choosing not to hand the system a bad measurement is the harder call and it is the right one.

The file agrees with you and adds nothing to it. The 18:30 fetch shows no activity at all today — the newest thing in it is still Saturday's five-minute CFF16. Today's RT19 sits on the calendar as planned event 131228736, load 45, with nothing attached to it, and because there is no run for it to have failed to attach to, this is a clean skip rather than the pairing glitch that follows an early stop. Tomorrow's 05:20 hygiene pass clears the stale entry by itself.

So there is no deep-dive tonight and I am not going to manufacture one. No rep-by-rep, no heart-rate story, no verdict on your threshold — there is no trace to read, and inventing paces would be far worse than saying that plainly.

One thing did get logged: mobhip and mob9090, both ticked, a day before week 13's mobility placement formally starts. Neither is a training session and neither counts anywhere. You did them on the day you did nothing else, and that is worth a line.
recap.takeaways:
1) TUNE: NOT COMPUTED, AND THE ANCHORS HOLD — WHICH IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME, NOT A FAILURE. Today was a tune day by prescription, but there was no activity, so there was nothing for tune.py to read: no tune line in the pipeline log for 30 Aug, no tune report on disk, and the 18:30 job itself ran clean. zones.json stands exactly as tune.py wrote it on 30 July — FTP 236 W, bike LTHR 159, run threshold 4:22/km, run LTHR 167. The useful consequence: week 13's plan was written warning that Wednesday's RF6, Friday's RCI3 and Sunday's RAe10 might all shift tonight. They do not. Every run pace printed on the board is right as it stands.

2) ADAPT: RT19 CLASSIFIED SKIPPED, ABSORBED, NOT OWED. Cause is circumstance and it comes from your own dated note rather than from me inferring it. Rule applied: a skipped endurance session is only rescheduled when a natural same-intent slot exists without stacking, and there isn't one. The single pre-authored slot was last week's rule 4 — slide RT19 into Monday — but Monday is CF10 carrying the 165 W reference block, which week 13 explicitly protects from being moved or displaced. Put next to that, a threshold retest on your first day back from illness fails on its own merits, and 50/50 calls go to recover. So nothing was added, moved or rescheduled; week 13 is untouched.

3) THREE OF FIVE ENDURANCE SESSIONS ARE GONE FROM WEEK 12, AND I AM OPENING THAT RATHER THAN ABSORBING A FOURTH. RAn3 Thursday, CFF16 Saturday, RT19 today. Week 13's own rule 8 names two inside one week as the point where this wants a conversation. Two honest halves to it: the chronic-hole guard is deliberately NOT fired, because it exists for fatigue-caused failures and today's cause is illness — and firing it on a week that already carries only two hard sessions against a sustainable three would be exactly backwards. But three losses with three different explanations in one fortnight is a fact about the fortnight, not about the sessions, and it belongs to you rather than to an analyzer.

4) THE "2 SECONDS FASTER" REQUEST — LOGGED, NOT APPLIED, AND HERE IS THE HONEST WHY. zones.json is written only by tune.py from an actual measurement, never by hand; that invariant exists because a hardcoded FTP once survived two tunes and nine weeks of prescriptions were built on it. Beyond the rule, 2 s/km is smaller than the last measurement could resolve — 30 July moved threshold pace 260 to 262 and the file itself calls a step that size noise. The larger point underneath your request is the real one, though, and I think you are pointing at something true: the bike anchors are from 28 July, the run anchors from 30 July, and the Race-Specific phase now opens on five-week-old numbers in BOTH sports. The next scheduled bike tune is week 16. Accepting that wait, or adding a retest inside weeks 14–15, is a change to the grid and therefore your call — say the word and I will place one properly.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

Twenty-four minutes of Zone 3 in six-minute pieces, with recoveries only half as long as the work. That ratio is the instruction: these are meant to be repeatable, not maximal.
Set the number in the first ninety seconds of rep 1, then ride the same number four times. Rep four should be the same wattage as rep one. If it is not, rep one was wrong.
Do not ride the top of the band just because it is available. 248 W is 105% of FTP, and that is where 26 August's CT31 died — 238.9 W with heart rate nine beats over LTHR, and the tune was refused. 222–235 W is where this session lives.

end.name: CAe19 — 210′ long ride · the week's centrepiece
end.detail: Three and a half hours, of which 120 minutes are Zone 2 in four separate blocks. The 10′ Zone 1 breaks are structural, not optional — they are what stops four 30′ blocks becoming one long drift into Zone X. 196 W is the ceiling and Zone X starts one watt later.
end.desc:
10′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W → 4 × (30′ Zone 2 @ 165–196 W / 10′ Zone 1) → 40′ Zone 1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 30 Aug — the Zone 2 is NOT one continuous hold, and the ride ends on 40 minutes of Zone 1.)
This is what Race-Specific looks like. The adaptation being bought is substrate — producing real power on fat in hour three — and it cannot be bought in a shorter session at a higher intensity.
Take the 10-minute Zone 1 breaks properly, at 118–165 W and actually soft. They are what keep four 30-minute blocks from turning into one long drift.
196 W is the ceiling and Zone X starts one watt later. On a ride this long the most likely failure by far is fifteen unnoticed watts.
Eat and drink from the first hour, not the third. Three and a half hours is well past the point where the ride is decided by what is already in you.
If Monday's CF10 was missed, this is the fallback carrier for the 10′ @ 165 W block — its first Zone 2 hold runs 10:00 to 40:00, so minutes 20–30 fit. It is a weaker home: Saturday is four days after CCI3, outside the 3-day window the FTP-offset measurement needs.

end.name: RAe10 — 105′ long run
end.detail: Read the structure before you run it: only 45 of the 105 minutes are Zone 2, and the 35′ Zone 1 finish is the largest single segment. Finishing the last Zone 2 block and never coming back down is how this session goes wrong. Read the bands off zones.json in the morning.

10′ Zone 1 @ 5:45–7:17/km → 3 × (15′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km / 5′ Zone 1) → 35′ Zone 1. (Pulled live from the 80/20 library 30 Aug.)
This is not a 105-minute Zone 2 run. It is 45 minutes of Zone 2 inside 60 minutes of Zone 1, and the 35-minute Zone 1 finish is the largest single segment in it.
The classic error is finishing the last Zone 2 block and never coming back down, which turns the last half hour into Zone X and costs the week's ratio.
It follows yesterday's 210 minutes, and that cost is real but small where it lands. Only 45 minutes are at a pace worth defending, so the pre-fatigue mostly falls on the Zone 1, where it does no harm. If the Zone 2 blocks will not come to 5:01–5:45/km without forcing, run them at the slow end and let the Zone 1 carry the session — the volume is the point here, not the pace.
